title: How data centers are driving a US natural-gas boom
gist: The US AI data-center boom is driving a natural-gas resurgence: PJM's interconnection queue has shifted toward gas, Meta's Louisiana data center pushed its utility from three to 10 planned gas plants, and over 100 off-grid data-center power plants (115 GW) have been proposed. Hyperscaler emissions are rising sharply, with Meta up 45% and reevaluating its 2030 net-zero goal.

insights.claim: PJM, the largest US grid operator, accepted 715 projects totaling over 200 GW into its interconnection queue in August, with nearly half of that capacity being natural-gas plants.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Gas turbine makers, pipeline operators and gas producers serving PJM states benefit from the queue shift.
insights.locator: But there’s been a shift in some places

insights.claim: If every project in PJM's queue were built, the fossil-fuel share of PJM's grid would rise from 61% to 67%, per Purdue energy modeler Kevin Kircher.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Contradicts decarbonization trajectories; supports long-duration gas demand in the Mid-Atlantic/Midwest.
insights.locator: If all the projects in the queue were built

insights.claim: Interconnection queues, long dominated by cheaper wind and solar, are a leading indicator of the future grid mix, and in some regions they now show a pivot toward natural gas driven by data-center demand.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Track queue composition as a forward signal for generation equipment and fuel demand.
insights.locator: If you want to understand the future of the grid

insights.claim: Natural gas, already the largest US electricity source, has basically become the default way to meet exploding AI-driven power demand.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Positions gas as the marginal fuel of the AI buildout regardless of renewables' cost advantage.
insights.quote: the AI boom in the US is basically synonymous with a natural-gas boom

insights.claim: Plans for Meta's Louisiana data center have expanded such that the local utility went from three planned natural-gas plants to 10.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Single hyperscaler campuses can drive multi-plant utility gas buildouts.
insights.quote: The local utility went from three planned natural-gas plants to 10.

insights.claim: Meta's emissions rose 45% year over year per its 2026 Sustainability Report, versus increases at Google (18%), Amazon (16%) and Microsoft (25%), and Meta is 'reevaluating' its 2030 net-zero goal.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler climate targets are slipping under AI load; ESG-screened holders may reassess.
insights.locator: This AI-driven rush is already affecting

insights.claim: Meta said that when the grid cannot deliver power on the necessary timeline it will pursue other methods, including building its own on-site generation.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Grid interconnection delays are pushing hyperscalers toward behind-the-meter generation.
insights.locator: And there’s another tidbit in that Meta report

insights.claim: Over 100 off-grid power plants for data centers have been proposed in the US with a combined 115 GW of capacity—more than double California's peak demand—most proposed since the start of 2025.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: A large new market for on-site gas generation equipment outside utility rate bases.
insights.quote: more than double the entire peak power demand of California
insights.locator: Over 100 such facilities have been proposed

insights.claim: Alternatives such as wind and solar paired with batteries, and demand flexibility that curbs grid draw at peak, could meet rising demand, but the speed-to-power imperative is currently favoring gas.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Renewables-plus-storage and demand-response remain the upside alternative if gas supply chains bottleneck.
